headline: Shift grid costs to large energy users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of the costs for grid infrastructure and capacity, reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users, Dominion Energy (initially, due to amendments).
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these billions of dollars in costs from falling on residential ratepayers. Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration advocated for this change, which is expected to save Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Mandate data center water usage reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and aiding state water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups, water conservationists, Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ).
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales to data centers, separating potable and reclaimed water. This legislation, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to increase transparency and provide crucial data for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Regulate data center siting and noise
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for noise impacts on residential areas and schools, and to consider other environmental and community impacts before approving new data center developments.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters), local governments, Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Senator Danica A. Roem.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't.
news_summary: Virginia's new law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools. While it mandates studies and disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits, water caps, or setbacks, giving localities tools for evaluation rather than strict prohibitions.
